methodology.note: This is NOT the paper's (paper/SEMINAR.tex, "Narration and Synchronization") full proposed benchmark. It covers: (1) deterministic structural invariant checks, and (2) an LLM-judge rubric that PROXIES for MOS naturalness and notation/phonetic accuracy. It does not include real human MOS ratings, real ASR-based WER, or a comparison against the MathReader/Polly baselines the paper names — those require synthesized audio for all three systems plus an ASR pass and are not implemented here.

results.title: Inner product of two vectors
results.spokenText: Consider a vector a in n-dimensional real space and another vector b in n-dimensional real space. Their inner product is defined as gamma, equal to a transpose b.

fragments.spoken: Consider a vector a in n-dimensional real space
and another vector b in n-dimensional real space.
Their inner product is defined as gamma, equal to a transpose b.
fragments.boardText: Their inner product is defined as $\gamma = a^T b$.

results.title: Orthogonality condition
results.spokenText: The vector a transpose, multiplied by a sub perpendicular, equals zero.

fragments.spoken: The vector a transpose,
multiplied by a sub perpendicular, equals zero.

issues: The narration includes verbal filler ('The vector') which is not on the board.
Reading 'a^T' as 'a transpose' is correct, but 'multiplied by' is an unnecessary addition for juxtaposition.
The reading of 'a_perp' is slightly unnatural; it is standard to read it as 'a perp' rather than 'a sub perpendicular'.
